beats.text: In 1932, Australia sent soldiers with machine guns into a war against birds. And lost.
Twenty thousand emus had stormed the wheat fields of Western Australia.
So the army sent Major Meredith, two soldiers, two machine guns, and ten thousand bullets.
On day one, the emus simply ran out of range.
Two days later, he ambushed a thousand of them at a dam.
Luckily, he had a new plan: mount the gun on a truck.
Unluckily, emus can run fifty kilometres an hour, over ground no truck could handle.
You see, every flock posted a tall lookout.
The moment the guns appeared, they scattered in every direction, like trying to catch a bag of spilled marbles.
By December, the army claimed nine hundred and eighty-six birds, at roughly ten bullets each.
Meredith admitted the emus could face machine guns with the invulnerability of tanks.
The soldiers went home. The emus stayed.
And today, the emu is on Australia's coat of arms. Undefeated.
